steps.label: The definition
lines: The solubility product Ksp of a sparingly
soluble salt is the product of the molar
concentrations of its ions in a saturated
solution, each raised to the power of its
steps.why: Ksp is the equilibrium constant of the dissolution equilibrium — the solid's concentration is constant and drops out, leaving only the ion product.
common_mistakes: Defining Ksp for any solution. The definition holds for a SATURATED solution.
Leaving out the temperature. Like every equilibrium constant, Ksp is fixed only at a stated temperature.
steps.memory_tip: Saturated solution, ion concentrations multiplied, coefficients as powers.
steps.margin_note: Three keywords: sparingly soluble, saturated, product.

steps.label: The expression
lines: Precipitation starts when the ionic product
of the solution becomes greater than Ksp.
steps.why: The dissolution equilibrium is written first because the expression comes from it: solid AgCl is left out, and the two ions each appear to the power 1.
common_mistakes: Including [AgCl] in the expression. The solid is not included.
Writing the dissolution with a one-way arrow. A saturated solution is an equilibrium: ⇌.
steps.memory_tip: Solid out, ions in. For AgCl the expression is just the two ion concentrations multiplied.
steps.margin_note: The ionic-product comparison line links Ksp to precipitation.

insider_note: Definition and expression, one mark each, and the expression is checked for one omission before anything else. Write the dissolution equilibrium first and the expression falls out of it correctly.
